title: No Map, Just a Compass
html:
A friend once told me life is like navigating the woods at night with a dim flashlight. You can only ever see twelve inches in front of you. So, in effect, you can’t know where you’re going. All you can do is plot out your next step.

In an episode of Chris Williamson’s Modern Wisdom featuring Adam Grant, Adam said:

“I think it's not realistic to have a map in a dynamic and uncertain world. What's much more plausible is to have a compass, right? Which is to ask, is this the right next step? Does it feel directionally correct? Is it taking me closer to my values and my goals? Or is it moving me away from those? Is it making me more like the people that I admire or less like them? And I think that that compass is frankly all we need, and it's much more realistic than the perfect map.”

This seems like a perspective worth adopting for those who want something else for themselves than being a replaceable cog in a corporate machine. But I don’t mean to disparage those working in golden handcuffs. I actually think it might be optimal for some people because, at the end of the day, if you’re healthy, financially stable, and have love at hand, you’re winning. And the corporate world can enable you to achieve such things. However, I don’t suspect I’d fare well in the corporate world.

“But, if not the corporate world, then what?”

Since graduating high school in 2020, I’ve been asked some version of this question ad nauseam, and, for the past half-decade or so, my go-to response has been, “I have no idea. I just want to do something new and useful.”

“New” and “useful” have been my north poles. And, as Adam suggested, orienting myself towards them has helped me ask “Is this the right next step?” and “Is it taking me closer to my values and my goals? Or is moving me away from those?”

In the spirit of new and useful, I’ve been learning how to code, write, speak, empathize, explore, question, observe, etc — all in the hopes that I may one day assemble these skills to create something of great value. But I haven’t a clue what that might be.

I don’t have a map — just a compass.
